articles.title: Spygate saga continues to haunt Southampton as case drags on
articles.summary: Manager Tonda Eckert’s future remains in the balance with the FA yet to decide over a suitable punishment. Fifty seconds was all it took for the chant to begin. “You know what you are, you know what you are, cheating bastards, you know what you are,” bellowed the Bristol City fans, starting up a…
body: This is what life is now like for Southampton after May’s spying scandal – a saga whose full consequences are still unknown and could have ramifications for the season ahead. The English Football League acted swiftly after photographs emerged of a junior staff member hiding behind a tree to film a Middlesbrough training session, expelling Southampton from the Championship play-offs and deducting four points after the club admitted multiple spying offences, including on Oxford United and Ipswich. The Football Association’s case against Tonda Eckert, the manager, is taking far longer. And patience is wearing thin.

The incident left a deep stain on Southampton’s reputation, one that will take time to fade and will leave an indelible mark on their history. Fans initially felt a mixture of fury and embarrassment – their promotion hopes snatched away over smartphone footage of a rival’s training session. Still, it has not stopped them flocking to St Mary’s this season: attendances were a shade under 30,000 for visits from Stoke, Millwall and Swansea and a season-high of 30,132 made Saturday’s Bristol City match almost a sell-out.

articles.title: Ukraine's Koval joins new team after Russia controversy
articles.summary: Ukrainian basketball player Kate Koval has been granted a transfer waiver to join Baylor University after leaving Lousiana State because they signed a Russian player.
body: Ukrainian basketball player Kate Koval has joined a new college team after leaving Louisiana State University because they had signed a Russian player.
Koval, 20, was granted a transfer waiver by the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) at the request of LSU.
The waiver allowed Koval to join a new team despite the transfer window closing in April, and she has signed with Baylor University in Texas.
Koval played in all 35 of LSU's matches last season, averaging 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.

articles.title: ‘I want Teófimo’: Ryan Garcia calls out rivals after two-round destruction of Conor Benn
articles.summary: Garcia stops Benn 1min 25sec into second round. Champion floors challenger with concussive right. López, Haney, Stevenson among possible fights. Ryan Garcia needed less than four minutes to blow away Conor Benn before turning his sights on the rest of the welterweight division.
body: The 28-year-old American demolished Benn inside two rounds on Saturday night to retain his World Boxing Council championship at 147lb, dropping the British challenger with a concussive right hand before the referee stepped in moments later at T-Mobile Arena. The sensational finish ignited the mostly pro-Garcia crowd of 18,855 on Mexican Independence Day weekend. Then, with Teófimo López taunting him from ringside and threatening to storm the ring, Garcia made it clear he was ready to take on all comers.

“We got to clear this [division] out,” said Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs), who was making the first defense of the welterweight title he won by flooring and outpointing Mario Barrios at the same arena in February.

Benn (25-2, 14 KOs), who had promised “tenacity, ferocity, spite” throughout an acrimonious build-up and vowed to pressure Garcia from the first bell, made good on that pledge. He set a frenetic pace in the opening frame, bolting from his corner and dragging Garcia into heavy exchanges. Benn scored well to the body and caught the champion with a shot to the back of the head that went unpunished, while Garcia repeatedly threw his signature left hook in an ominous statement of intent.

articles.title: What is going wrong at Glentoran this season?
articles.summary: A Glentoran side that, on paper, promised so much before the season started has so far failed to deliver in the Irish Premiership, so what is going wrong?
body: The Glens have won just two of their opening six league matches and already find themselves nine points behind current league leaders Coleraine, who they face on Tuesday.

But why has it gone so wrong for the Glens so far this season?
Glentoran had recorded their highest points tally of owner Ali Pour's ownership last season, while striker Pat Hoban enjoyed a prolific debut campaign.

articles.title: 'Tough to control emotions' as Sabalenka suffers another near miss
articles.summary: After losing another Grand Slam final, Aryna Sabalenka smashes her racquet in frustration at a year that has seen her lose her world number one status.
body: Aryna Sabalenka cut a forlorn figure as she sat staring into space following a painful defeat by Elena Rybakina in the US Open final.
As Rybakina celebrated her third Grand Slam title following a 6-4 5-7 6-2 win in New York, cameras pictured Sabalenka deep in thought as she sat in silence with her team.
At a tournament which has delivered so much success for two-time champion Sabalenka, the disappointment the 28-year-old has faced in the past week leaves her with plenty to ponder.
Not only has Rybakina replaced Sabalenka as the world number one after 99 weeks at the summit, she has now ended the Belarusian's 20-match winning streak at Flushing Meadows.

articles.title: FastPasses, Mega Honey Deuces and $55 chopped cheese: welcome to the US Open in 2041 | Bryan Armen Graham
articles.summary: Craig Tiley says the US Open is going to become the ‘Disneyland of tennis’, and he means it aspirationally. Here’s what that might look like 15 years from now. The year is 2041 and you’ve successfully made it through security and onto the grounds of the USTA Liquid Death National Tennis Center.
body: It’s been 15 years since Craig Tiley first used that shorthand before the 2026 US Open, barely a month after taking over as chief executive of the United States Tennis Association. Longtime Open-goers had already adopted it as gallows humor, muttering it between expletives on the outer courts during qualifying week, which for another few years was still free. That Tiley meant it aspirationally told you everything you needed to know about where New York’s annual late-summer orgy of sport, fashion and conspicuous consumption was headed.

Tiley’s grand vision was a future US Open with more entertainment, more extracurriculars and more “opportunities” for children and adults to experience things. At a tournament where the once-humble grounds pass already fetched hundreds of dollars on the resale market and chicken nuggets flecked with Petrossian caviar went for $100, the natural question was: more what?

We now know. Layers of access. Premium seating. Branded activations. An incremental, almost imperceptible erosion of value-for-money not seen in American life since the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978.

articles.title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.
body: Kazakhstan's Rybakina produced a brilliant performance to beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 in Saturday's final and repeat her Australian Open success against the same player in January.
Clutching the trophy on Saturday night, Rybakina reflected that "some magic is happening" for her after her difficult lead-in to the tournament.
The 27-year-old aggravated a foot injury during her quarter-final in Cincinnati against Iga Swiatek last month, a little over a week before the final major of the year began.

Playing on through injury could have had dire consequences for the rest of her season - but Rybakina, knowing the top ranking was in her grasp, wanted to try and play in the final Grand Slam of the year.

articles.title: Serie A: Napoli vs. Bologna – Probable line-ups and where to watch on TV
articles.summary: Early pressure is creeping up on both Massimiliano Allegri and Domenico Tedesco ahead of Sunday evening’s Serie A clash between Napoli and Bologna, which will be available to watch for free on the BBC for viewers in the UK.
body: Allegri began his career as Napoli head coach with a 2-0 win away against Genoa in the opening round of 2026-27 Serie A fixtures, but he has since gone on to lose his last three matches across all competitions in a tough run of fixtures against Como, Inter and Arsenal across the league and Champions League.

Bologna are still looking for their first competitive victory under new head coach Tedesco, but picked up their first point of the season with a 2-2 draw at home against Sassuolo last weekend. They come into tonight’s game in 16th place.

Napoli will be without Scott McTominay until the international break. Kevin De Bruyne is expected to continue starting in the Scot’s place. Billy Gilmour is expected to join the Belgian and Stanislav Lobotka in midfield, although Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa has recently returned to training and could return in the coming weeks. Antonio Vergara is also expected to feature at some stage.

articles.summary: Elena Rybakina cemented her position as world No 1 by dethroning two-time US Open winner Aryna Sabalenka to seal her maiden title in New York.
body: Rybakina ​won ‌her ​first US Open, beating top seed ‌and defending champion ⁠Sabalenka ​6-4 ​5-7 ⁠6-2 on Arthur Ashe Stadium.
The 27-year-old had already been guaranteed to replace Sabalenka at No 1 in the rankings next week.
Sabalenka was looking to become only the third woman to achieve a New York 'three-peat' in the Open era, after Chris Evert and Serena Williams.
Instead she was left sat in her chair, furiously smashing her racket in to smithereens as Rybakina, from Kazakhstan, celebrated a third Grand Slam title.

articles.title: Guimaraes haunts Sunderland as Arsenal continue winning start
articles.summary: Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal two minutes after David Raya had saved a penalty as Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 to move above Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.
body: The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half, a decision which enraged Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

Arsenal had to withstand late pressure from the home side, with Raya saving well from Nordi Mukiele, but they made the result safe when Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty after Reinildo Mandava was shown a second yellow card for hauling him down.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.
